policy.purpose: Preserve discussion ideas and retrieve them at new-proof or blockage reviews; remembered ideas are not evidence.
policy.capture: Record substantive new ideas with origin/date, assumptions, test, failure boundary and revisit trigger. Preserve IDs and append dated reviews for later dispositions; never erase contrary evidence. English paraphrases of Korean discussion.
retrieval_triggers: Before scoping a new proof or physical candidate
At a named blocker or REVIEW_REQUIRED decision
When new sources or counterexamples change a load-bearing assumption
policy.retrieval_record: At a logical checkpoint, record selected idea IDs, relevant gate, changed input, minimal test, use/defer reason and revisit condition in the existing exploration ledger. If none is relevant, record NONE and reason rather than manufacture another attempt.
policy.promotion: No idea is an adopted model, source owner, theorem or observation. New models require separate version/hash/assumption/falsifier admission under existing governance.
policy.continuation: Retrieval does not authorize model/rate/state/time changes, automatic weakened successors, external contact or an exhaustive search.
policy.proof_economy: No per-idea PDF or new result ID without an actual scientific gate closure.

ideas.title: Cosmic formation as a phase transformation of one microscopic system
ideas.origin: Operator, 2026-11-12: use the TECT viewpoint to identify a starting point, not arbitrary model shopping.
ideas.hypothesis: The observed spacetime-matter regime could be a phase of a more basic system; not an explosion into pre-existing empty space.
ideas.support: Scoped R-158 conditional transition; F3 is an OPEN cosmological target, not evidence for cosmic origin.
ideas.unproved: Microscopic carrier/law, phase discriminator, energy scale, time/causal emergence and independent observations.
ideas.test: Extract transition variables and assumed background from exact authorities; scope one separately versioned hypothesis with a rejecting test.
ideas.failure_boundary: Reject that candidate if its claimed emergent space/time is inserted or its distinct phases cannot be physically distinguished; not all TECT hypotheses.
ideas.revisit_when: New phase-candidate scoping or a new physical control-quantity input.

ideas.title: Pregeometric phase without externally prescribed physical time
ideas.origin: Operator, 2026-11-12: a different universe without time might structurally precede the current one.
ideas.hypothesis: A microscopic regime may not initially admit the operational clocks and metric time of the observed phase.
ideas.support: Conceptual motivation only; no physical timeless phase has been established here.
ideas.unproved: State/constraint law, relational observables, phase comparison and usable clock emergence; structural precedence is not chronological before.
ideas.test: Define a relational clock criterion without importing the physical time to be derived.
ideas.failure_boundary: A hidden proper-time parameter, a stationary state called timeless, or a clock rescaling is not a derivation.
ideas.revisit_when: A candidate supplies a relational state law and a concrete clock diagnostic.

ideas.title: Possible loss of effective temporal structure at extreme curvature
ideas.origin: Operator, 2026-11-12: could time progressively disappear inside a black hole?
ideas.hypothesis: Extreme-curvature physics might require a phase where an effective clock/metric description fails.
ideas.support: Motivation only. Ordinary event-horizon crossing and distant-observer redshift do not establish loss of the infaller's proper time.
ideas.unproved: Invariant threshold, coupled microscopic gravitational law, temporal diagnostic and a collapse-to-phase map.
ideas.test: Separate redshift, finite proper-time geodesic incompleteness, destruction of particular clocks and failure of any effective temporal description.
ideas.failure_boundary: An event horizon or coordinate singularity identified with timelessness without an invariant argument is inadmissible evidence.
ideas.revisit_when: A gravitationally coupled candidate supplies an invariant temporal diagnostic.

ideas.title: Possible common phase in otherwise inaccessible regimes
ideas.origin: Operator, 2026-11-12: black-hole interiors and beyond the universe's end might share a physical state.
ideas.hypothesis: An independently defined inaccessible regime could share a microscopic phase with a pregeometric candidate.
ideas.support: No established equivalence; an observational horizon is not a demonstrated edge of space.
ideas.unproved: Definitions of both regions and a common invariant state/phase mapping.
ideas.test: Define the boundary without assuming a spatial edge, then compare invariants under one law.
ideas.failure_boundary: Shared inaccessibility does not imply equal physical state; undefined outside means defer, not cosmic theorem.
ideas.revisit_when: A candidate supplies both boundary definitions and a testable common-state map.

ideas.title: Geometry and matter from common microscopic degrees of freedom
ideas.origin: Earlier operator discussion in this thread; registered 2026-11-12.
ideas.hypothesis: One law could produce geometric/material observables and their energy-momentum transfer without spurious inertial drag.
ideas.support: Unifying objective, not identity of mass, energy, momentum and geometry as the same physical quantity.
ideas.unproved: Observable maps, symmetry/conservation, inertial/interacting response, physical time, metric and causal limits.
ideas.test: Require one fixed law to give distinct geometric/material observables and consistent exchange; do not relabel a mass term as derived gravity.
ideas.failure_boundary: Unwanted inertial friction or incompatible response laws reject the explicitly scoped candidate.
ideas.revisit_when: A shared physical dynamics/observable packet appears.

ideas.title: Physical origin of a TECT phase-control quantity
ideas.origin: Collaborator extraction from R-157/R-158, prompted by the operator on 2026-11-12.
ideas.hypothesis: A justified microscopic conserved quantity or exchange law might turn R-158's imposed ensemble into a physical effective description.
ideas.support: R-158: fixed-torus Q=||Psi||_2^2/2 or Omega_mu=F_P1-mu Q transition. R-157: original neutral-branch restriction. Both preserved.
ideas.unproved: Physical Q, origin of mu, actual evolution and invariant spatial order parameter; the saturating plane wave is not a derived density crystal.
ideas.test: Audit a candidate symmetry/exchange law before any phase sweep; do not insert mu(t) merely to force a transition.
ideas.failure_boundary: Missing physical conservation/exchange or retrospective control fitting fails admission, not the conditional R-158 theorem.
ideas.revisit_when: Next phase-input review or genuinely new source-owned conservation/exchange packet.

ideas.title: Dynamical laboratory gauge links as reference mechanisms
ideas.origin: TECT-PHY-001 source intake, narrowed after operator clarification, 2026-11-12.
ideas.hypothesis: A matter/link experiment can clarify the requirements for an interaction-time-readout packet.
ideas.support: Three versioned sources, one independently reviewed reference in PHY-001.
ideas.unproved: Any PAH identity or spacetime-generation relevance; the experiments already assume space, time and external control.
ideas.test: Compare multiple preparation-dependent responses under one fixed source law, not programmed replay.
ideas.failure_boundary: Gauge notation or a trace match does not make a cosmological candidate.
ideas.revisit_when: A physical microscopic candidate needs an interaction/readout audit; not an automatic successor.

ideas.title: Internal conversion as a source of phase control
ideas.origin: Operator requests creative theory construction after PHY-002, 2026-11-12; collaborative unadopted design.
ideas.hypothesis: A closed parent with interconverting sectors could supply a phase-control quantity without a fitted external chemical-potential history.
ideas.support: R158 identifies the missing physical control input; the design is a new hypothesis, not an existing microscopic realization.
ideas.unproved: Physical reservoir/state, exact transfer and stability, compatible effective reduction, time and domain. A pair-conversion term may change the full Hessian and classical zero may remain invariant.
ideas.test: After separate model admission, test symmetry and genuine exchange, then the coupled zero-phase Hessian against the R158 ensemble before any large simulation.
ideas.failure_boundary: No silent scalar-mu identification, coherent-state assumption, deleted reservoir memory, counterterm rescue or inherited A2 physical time.

ideas.title: Network order and mobile defects as shared microscopic variables
ideas.origin: Creative alternative requested by operator, 2026-11-12; read-only design critique.
ideas.hypothesis: Extended connectivity order and persistent mobile defects might become different collective descriptions of one rewiring system.
ideas.support: A prospective single-rule graph design is recorded; existing graph literature is reference only and supplies no TECT identity.
ideas.unproved: State selection, absence of clustering, dimension, locality, mobile excitations and physical time. Valence, vertex count and graph cycles are not dimension, mass or P1 charge.
ideas.test: Compare extended graphs against dense block competitors under the same full Hamiltonian before any broad simulation.
ideas.failure_boundary: A clustering-favored graph state is not generated space; no post-hoc rescue term or direct Sector-A inheritance.
ideas.revisit_when: Separate new-model admission only if this adds geometric explanatory value beyond the higher-reuse phase-control route.

ideas.title: Symmetric tensor reservoir without internal pair-source cancellation
ideas.origin: Separate ALT001 prospective-model intake authorized by operator, 2026-11-12.
ideas.hypothesis: A weight-two symmetric tensor reservoir can couple to the full pair tensor instead of its cancelling scalar contraction.
ideas.support: Exact source norm, weighted transfer and same-sector initial second-response improvement verified in ALT001; not overall physical superiority.
ideas.unproved: Same-state actual stability superiority, physical state/carrier, full P1 symmetry, limiting behavior and value of six complex reservoir coordinates versus one.
ideas.test: After separate admission, compare actual constrained/rotating stability for explicitly matched reservoir states without favorable orientation selection.
ideas.failure_boundary: No first-order charge response at zero reservoir; no invariant scalar dark-sector or all-time dominance claim; no conditional averaging or state deletion.
